key_insight: Tree-search branches in LLM reasoning often become redundant, so the paper uses sibling-action uncertainty to decide both which branches to keep and how much budget to spend on them.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper, faster multi-step LLM search with large token and latency savings while preserving accuracy, making reasoning systems more cost-efficient in practice.
method: Measure semantic dispersion among sibling actions as a proxy for downstream uncertainty.
Use uncertainty-aware pruning to drop low-promise candidates before expansion.
Use uncertainty-aware budgeting to allocate fewer samples to low-uncertainty subtrees and more to high-uncertainty ones.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reportedly cuts token usage by up to 90% and latency by up to 9× at comparable accuracy, generalizing across four tree search algorithms and both open- and closed-source LLMs.
watch_item: The budget rule depends on dispersion being a reliable uncertainty signal, so performance may degrade when semantic similarity is a poor proxy for true reasoning diversity or answer entropy.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
